items.claim: The row discloses and rejects the ish-tie to the following verse but never discloses the equally salient shared-token tie to the preceding verse, where Prov.29.25's בַּיהוָ֣ה and Prov.29.26's וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה both carry the sparse book-wide יהוה token.
items.evidence: Skeleton sweep for יהוה (any prefix form) across Prov.25-29 returns only 6 of 133 verses (Prov.25.22, 28.5, 28.25, 29.13, 29.25, 29.26), so the 29.25/29.26 adjacency is one of only three such consecutive-verse pairs invoking Yahweh's name in the whole Hezekiah collection, not a generic-noun case like the disclosed ish-tie to 29.27; the row's asymmetric engagement (one neighbor addressed, the other silent) is a cross-seam disclosure gap, though single_proverb remains the defensible call since both cases are thematic/lexical echoes, not construction-run cohesion. Separately, "in this part" in the observed_substrate_signals is scoped ambiguously between the C5 collection and the writer's own P12 tiling span (Prov.28.1-29.27) -- the digit is identical either way (4 root-II occurrences: Prov.28.15, 29.2, 29.12, 29.26, confirmed by direct byte read against the root-I mishle/mashal homograph that a naive skeleton sweep would otherwise conflate) but the phrasing itself skirts the file-order/positional-reference register rule.

items.claim: The chiastic mutual-abomination reading of Prov.29.27 (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר דָּֽרֶךְ) is byte-accurate, its single-witness PE and C5-collection-close position are correctly disclosed as corroboration only, and the ish-tie to 29.26 is correctly named and rejected as a generic token.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.29.27 and nowhere between 29.26 and 30.1 otherwise; prov_device_inventory.json confirms the C5/C6 seam is additionally carried by the tier-1 divrei/massa header spine at Prov.30.1, so the collection-close boundary this row shares with its neighbor is doubly warranted (PE plus header) without overclaiming either side's evidence.

items.claim: The row's headline digit for "the term for 'words of'" (19 verses book-wide) blends the construct state דברי ("words of X") with unrelated suffixed and absolute-plural forms of the same root, so the named object and the swept digit do not match even though the downstream 5-of-19 and 2-of-5 sub-fractions still hold.
items.evidence: A skeleton sweep for דברי returns 19 verses, but byte review shows only 9 are genuine construct-state "words of X" (Prov.1.6, 12.6, 18.4, 18.8, 22.12, 22.17, 26.22, 30.1, 31.1); the other 10 are differently-pointed forms of the same root -- 1cs/2ms/3ms-suffixed "my/your/his words" (including this row's own cited verse, Prov.30.6, whose דְּבָרָ֑יו is "his words," not a construct) or absolute-plural "words" (Prov.10.19, 24.26, 26.6, 29.19) -- a blended sweep the toolkit's own semantic-class-count-discipline rule forbids. The verse-initial subset of 5 (matching prov_device_inventory.json's divrei_verse_initial list) and the 2-header subset remain correct as reported, since all 5 verse-initial hits happen to be true construct forms; only the top-line 19 and its "words of" gloss are mismatched.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative engages a tangential dispute about how many things 30:8-9 unpacks rather than the strongest real rival to this row's own boundary: merging Prov.30.7-9 (שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת...) with the preceding Prov.30.1-6 Agur unit, since both are first-person Agur material separated only by a tier-3 petuchah the campaign rule itself says is never a driver.
items.evidence: Prov.30.7 opens a direct 2nd-person petition register ("I have asked of YOU") distinct from 30.1-6's 3rd-person narration plus 1st-person confession of ignorance -- a genuine register shift that is the actual strongest warrant for the seam, stronger than the clause-counting dispute the row instead rejects. The row's own boundary call (splitting at the Prov.30.6 petuchah) is independently defensible on this register-shift ground, but that ground is never stated, leaving the row's disclosed rival weaker than the real one.

items.claim: The four-verse דור anaphora at Prov.30.11-14 is byte-verified as a genuine construction-run (דּ֭וֹר / דּ֭וֹר / דּ֭וֹר / דּ֤וֹר open each verse in turn), the closing sword-sense חרבות is correctly distinguished from the Prov.17.1 dry-morsel homograph per the toolkit's own hazard catalog, and the PE close at 30.14 (not before) is accurately disclosed as corroboration only.
items.evidence: Direct byte read of oshb Prov.30.11-30.14 confirms the verse-initial דור token at all four verses (4 of 4), matching the row's own claim; pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.30.14 only, with no mark at 30.11-30.13, correctly leaving the front boundary (against Prov.30.10's unrelated servant/slander saying) resting on the anaphora alone rather than a fabricated mark.

items.claim: The leech numerical saying at Prov.30.15-16 correctly names the chapter's first three/four formula and its four listed items completed only at 30.16, and correctly keeps the numeral opener and its list together per the list-by-function chunking rule rather than fabricating a mark it does not have.
items.evidence: Direct read of oshb/WEB Prov.30.15-16 confirms Sheol, the barren womb, the earth, and fire as the four items named at 30.16 (4 of 4); no three/four numeral formula precedes it anywhere in Prov.30.1-14 (direct read of the full span); pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE only at Prov.30.14 (the unit's open) with none at 30.15 or 30.16, and the row correctly does not claim a closing mark it lacks, relying instead on the list's own completion.

items.claim: The English rendering attached to oshb:Prov.30.20 is WEB-verbatim (“So is the way of an adulterous woman”, web:Prov.30.20) except for capitalization, but the row presents it in straight quotes tagged only oshb:Prov.30.20, not the curly quotes plus in-field web: ref the toolkit mandates for verbatim WEB text.
items.evidence: web:Prov.30.20 clean text opens “So is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats...”, matching the row's straight-quoted gloss word-for-word aside from case; check_web_quotes.py only scans curly-quoted spans against adjacent web: refs, so this straight-quoted instance passed the automated gate silently -- exactly the failure mode the tool exists to catch. The underlying five-fold דרך catchword-chain argument across 30.19-20 is otherwise byte-verified and sound (four verse-initial occurrences in 30.19 plus the fifth reopening 30.20), and the K/Q disclosure at Prov.30.18 (unpointed ketiv immediately preceding its pointed qere) is byte-accurate.

items.claim: The three/four formula at Prov.30.21-23 correctly assigns two items per verse across 30.22-23, correctly keeps the numeral and its list whole per the list-by-function rule, and its petuchah brackets at 30.20/30.23 are accurately disclosed.
items.evidence: oshb/WEB cross-check confirms the four items (servant becoming king and a fool filled with food in 30.22; an unloved woman married and a maidservant supplanting her mistress in 30.23); pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.30.20 and Prov.30.23 exactly matching the row's two citations, with none at 30.21 or 30.22 (correctly not claimed).
